pairs: all unordered distinct pairs, A < B
initial_conditions: every binary state at each ring width
continuation_actions: at every synchronous tick choose globally either A or B
budget: exactly h continuation ticks; all 2^h open-loop words, no early stopping
metrics: prepared-state Hamming distance and noncommutation count
number of distinct reachable outcomes per preparation
counts of equal sets, strict containment in either direction, and incomparable sets
counts of equal-size but different outcome sets
fraction of action words with different outcomes under the two preparations
counts of equal outcome sets but different action-to-outcome maps
witness_selection: first lexicographic (n,A,B,h,S) witness per observation for strict containment, equal-size/different-sets, and equal-sets/different-response-map; require h > 0 and differing prepared states
checks: integer CA maps agree with the vectorized engine for all n=6 panel states
same prepared state implies identical continuation maps and outcome sets
h=0 identity set discrepancy equals noncommutation
identity/constant-rule controls agree with explicit word enumeration
every saved witness independently replays through the vectorized engine
reporting: Aggregate exact integer counts by width, pair, horizon, and observation. Keep widths separate; cases and horizons are not independent samples. Save all selected witnesses, configuration and script hashes, environment versions, and a generated summary/figure.
limitations: Finite rings, a selected rule panel, and six-tick continuation budgets; no thermodynamic or open-endedness claim.
Possibilities are defined by an external open-loop controller; this is not intrinsic autonomy, learned adaptation, or a viability measure.
Different preparations have different complete present states; historical effects are carried by those states.
The action alphabet depends on the pair; do not rank pairs as having intrinsically greater freedom.
Population count can merge physically distinct outcomes; equality under it is weaker than equality of full states.
No hypothesis of life, criticality, or ethical desirability is tested by repertoire size alone.
